page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is provisioned with 2 vCPUs backed by a single physical Intel Xeon 8269CY core operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz with hyperthreading enabled. The instance provides 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It relies entirely on external network-attached storage without local disks, includes zero bundled graphics accelerators, and maintains a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate modest computational throughput, consistent with its single physical core constraint. Single-threaded metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1144.0 and a stress-ng rating of 1298.79, land in the bottom 25th percentile. Multi-threaded processing scores, such as PassMark CPU at 2133.1 and Geekbench multi-core at 1370.0, sit in the bottom 10th percentile. Memory throughput tests show 96.46 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 13.08 GB/sec for uncached 256MB reads, reflecting baseline DDR4 bus capabilities.

Hardware tradeoffs focus on high memory density per compute thread at an accessible cost entry point, sacrificing high compute performance. Instruction support includes AVX-512 extensions and hardware AES encryption. The instance suits lightweight in-memory caching tiers, small relational databases, staging environments, and backend microservices that demand moderate memory headroom without heavy CPU cycles.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.large is a memory-optimized instance running on the x86_64 architecture with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single Intel Xeon 8269CY physical core clocked at 2.5 GHz. It includes 16.0 GB of RAM, offering a high 8 GB per vCPU ratio, with no local ephemeral storage and no GPU accelerators. Networking is configured with a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth. In benchmark testing, the instance records lower-tier computational marks, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 1370.0 and PassMark CPU score of 2133.1, reflecting its single-core hyperthreaded setup. Despite restrained compute throughput, it provides stable memory capacity with 13.08 GB/sec large-block read bandwidth. This configuration is best suited for memory-reliant workloads with low concurrent compute demands, such as small Redis caches, development databases, and background memory-intensive utilities.
